name: QuIP# (Hadamard incoherence processing + E8 lattice codebooks)
bits: 2, 3 and 4-bit weight-only (<=4 bits per weight); activations fp16
activation_scheme: None. Weight-only PTQ. The mechanism is INCOHERENCE PROCESSING: an orthogonal transform (randomized Hadamard) is applied so weights and activations become approximately incoherent (spherically symmetric, sub-Gaussian with low maximum coherence), which is what makes very low bit grids viable. Then E8-lattice vector-quantization codebooks exploit that ball-shaped sub-Gaussian distribution.
kernels: quip-sharp reference implementation (Cornell-RelaxML); hardware-efficient E8 codebooks chosen specifically to be decodable in few integer ops.
quality_delta: The abstract claims 'state-of-the-art results in extreme compression regimes (<=4 bits per weight)', 'enables new behaviors in PTQ scaling', and 'supports fast inference', with no numeric perplexity in the abstract. No number recorded.
notes: GROUP SIZE LEFT NULL 2026-10-04: QuIP# is incoherence processing (randomized Hadamard) plus E8 LATTICE CODEBOOKS. A lattice codebook has no shared scale over a group of weights; the incoherence transform is what makes a fixed lattice work. Its precision levels (2/3/4-bit) are not group widths. Enum mismatch: 'hqq' is the closest existing value (both use learned/optimized codebooks). Two things worth carrying forward. First, QuIP# is a successor to QuIP v1 (Chee et al. 2023); the v1 preprint was not retrievable this session and is NOT recorded - do not create a separate quip record claiming details from the v2 paper. Second, the incoherent-rotations idea is the same family as QuaRot and SpinQuant and is the reason W4A4 became plausible at all: rotate, then quantize. Where SpinQuant LEARNS the rotation and QuIP#/QuaRot use a fixed or randomized Hadamard, that difference is the substantive distinction among the three.
